scope: Read-only compatibility research; no OS, ACL, sandbox or backend changes performed.
observations: Both C# projects identify the installed SDK and initialize LSP, then fail OpenProjectAsync while NamedPipeClientStream.TryConnect throws UnauthorizedAccessException.
This is semantic-workspace failure after initialization, not successful native C# IDE acceptance.

primary_sources.supports: Windows AppContainer named pipes require LOCAL namespace and same-container communication.
Current upstream creates a GUID pipe name and always starts/contacts an out-of-process BuildHost; no name override switch found in this implementation.
Windows pipe name is passed through unchanged; .NET Core clients/servers use CurrentUserOnly.
Pinned csharp-ls project loading uses MSBuildWorkspace and OpenProjectAsync; no documented in-process/pipe-name switch was found in CLI/settings.
MSBuild CLI in-process controls concern dotnet CLI execution; they do not change Roslyn BuildHostProcessManager source behavior.
Closed ProcessContainer schema enumerates capabilities/captureDenials/filesystem/learningMode/leastPrivilege/network/ui; no named-pipe grant is defined.
Open triaged upstream report reproduces AppContainer/MXC/SDK10 named-pipe access denial. An issue report is corroboration, not a released fix.

The pinned pre-BuildHost loader directly evaluates and builds Microsoft.Build project instances with design-time settings and SkipCompilerExecution. This avoids the observed MSBuildWorkspace BuildHost path; other MSBuild task IPC remains unverified.
--languageserver explicitly selects LSP stdio rather than OmniSharp's other stdio protocol.
The net6.0 driver specifies RollForward=LatestMajor. The installed archive runtimeconfig and selected isolated runtime must still be checked before claiming compatibility.
1.40.0 changes project loading to Roslyn BuildHost and removes direct Microsoft.Build dependencies; blindly choosing latest does not retain the candidate loader.
Live release metadata supplies the candidate's full commit, official asset size and SHA-256 digest.

explicit_backend_candidate.runtime: First verify archive runtimeconfig with the existing isolated .NET 10 host. Do not install an older runtime merely from the net6 asset name; direct loading and MSBuild/SDK compatibility require actual logs.
required_acceptance: Pin/verify official archive and extracted backend hashes; use explicit host-selected profile, never automatic fallback.
Use the same native process-container route, source read-only grants, external caches and network-deny policy.
Verify semantic workspace loading, symbols, hover/completion, diagnostics, formatting/refactor previews and cross-project separation against both fixtures; initialize alone is insufficient.
Retain backend logs, missing-capability UNAVAILABLE outcomes, unversioned diagnostics status, and source hashes.
Do not load repository OmniSharp/plugin settings as trusted Odin host configuration. A candidate source branch is not a sandbox compatibility proof.
explicit_backend_candidate.handoff: Primary source links, official release pin/digest and the proposed explicit profile were sent to root and platform_implementation. Platform owns actual installation and native matrix execution.

inference: The observed failure strongly fits AppContainer named-pipe namespace/security compatibility, rather than SDK presence or source/cache file grants. LOCAL naming is a relevant requirement, not a proven sufficient fix; same-container identities, CurrentUserOnly security and actual workspace operations still require verification.
not_run: Kernel object/security trace proving the exact deny decision
Patched upstream Roslyn build or alternative explicitly selected backend
Successful C# semantic workspace operation inside the native OS boundary
